articles.title: DP World Tour: Which players are missing from the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and who can still win the Race to Dubai?
articles.summary: Who is playing in the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship? A look at who is missing from the field for the first of two DP World Tour Play-Offs and which players remain in the running to top the season-long Race to Dubai standings; watch the conclusion to the season live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Only the top 70 available players in the season-long Race to Dubai standings will feature at Yas Links, the first of two events in the Middle East for the DP World Tour Play-Offs.

The entry list was released on Monday after the conclusion of the regular season ahead of the tournament taking place from November 5-8, live on Sky Sports , with 10 eligible players not named in the field.

Several of those not involved have previously expressly safety concerns about playing the season-ending events in the Middle East, with ‌Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia heightening fears of a wider regional conflict.

Fitzpatrick sits 10th in the Race to Dubai standings and is set to defend his DP World Tour Championship the following week, having defeated Rory McIlroy in a play-off last year to claim the trophy for a third time.

Speaking about the possibility of playing in the Middle East, Fitzpatrick said at last month's BMW PGA Championship: "No, I wouldn't be that comfortable.

"If the [DP World] Tour does go, I'm sure they have had the best advice possible on what that looks like. As things stand right now, I wouldn't necessarily be too keen on going."

Open champion Ryan Fox is the highest-ranked player in the Race to Dubai standings not playing in Abu Dhabi, although the New Zealander is currently still scheduled to feature at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

"I'm obviously of the opinion that the Tour is doing their due diligence," Fox said last month. "If they feel like it's safe for us to go, I'm willing to support that. But I can understand, also, why guys have some reservations."

Lowry (16th), Alex Fitzpatrick (24th), Min Woo Lee (38th), Ludvig Åberg (45th), MacIntyre (56th), Si Woo Kim (62nd), Rose (69th) and Ryan Gerard (70th) are the other eligible players not listed in the field.

The UK's Foreign Office doesn't currently have any restrictions to travel to the region , although updated guidelines on the government website warns those travelling "should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions".

The US government updated their travel advisories on Friday to "reflect the threat of increased Iranian-supported Houthi regional aggression". Their guidelines say travellers should "reconsider travel to the United Arab Emirates due to terrorism and armed conflict".

No player has to publicly specify whether their reason not to play is related to safety concerns or their own schedule, while only the top 50 available golfers after Abu Dhabi then progress to the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates a week later.

Race to Dubai battle heats up in Abu Dhabi

The top five players in the Race to Dubai standings are all currently scheduled to feature in Abu Dhabi, where the result is likely to play a key role in determining who ends the season and No 1 and lifts the Harry Vardon Trophy.

Eugenio Chacarra tops the standings by 669.27 points after winning the DP World India Championship, a third victory of the season, with Patrick Reed and McIlroy his two closest challengers.

Two-time DP World Tour winner Casey Jarvis and defending Abu Dhabi champion Aaron Rai complete the top five, where there's a $9m (£6.76m) prize purse and the winner picks up $1.53m (£1.15m).

Tommy Fleetwood won back-to-back Abu Dhabi titles in 2017 and 2018 and Tyrrell Hatton is also in the field, having previously won the 2021 edition, with both Englishmen and former world No 1 Adam Scott also in the field.

articles.title: Boomer women are dating after divorce. Men don’t always meet their standards.
articles.summary: “Baby-boom women setting divorce record” read the headline in The Washington Post. According to a 1992 study of U.S. Census data, women between the ages of 3...
articles.body:
Boomer women are dating after divorce. Men don’t always meet their standards.

"Baby-boom women setting divorce record" read the headline in The Washington Post. According to a 1992 study of U.S. Census data, women between the ages of 30 and 44 were "more likely to be divorced at some time in their lives than any group in American history."

The generation of women that brought us the sexual revolution and women's liberation also ushered in a new era of the American divorcée.

High divorce rates among boomer women have continued after the 1990s. According to an analysis of U.S. Census data conducted by Bowling Green State University, the annual divorce rate among Americans 65 and older more than tripled between 1990 and 2023. Today, nearly 1 in 6 seniors is divorced.

So what's it like to look for love as an older divorced person? Does a potentially larger dating pool make finding love easier? Are we living in a golden age for silver singles? How are they doing? And more specifically, how are they doing it? We reached out to several single seniors to find out.

Kristyne Haver, 69, dated for 18 solid years after she got divorced. "I was dating or semi-dating that whole time," Haver said from her office in Reading, Pennsylvania, where she works as a controller. "I've had some interesting situations."

For several years, she dated a dad in California who was separated from his wife but dragging his feet on getting divorced. On Facebook, she met another separated man in Missouri, but their online courtship ended when his wife started harassing her and her friends. She reconnected with a college boyfriend on LinkedIn who lived in Tampa, but ultimately decided that long-distance love wasn't for her.

"And of course, you get the younger guys looking for - what, a sugar mama or whatever?"

Not that Haver was opposed to age gaps. Over the years, she dated several younger men, including a Russian 25 years her junior whom she met in the parking lot of a grocery store, where she found him admiring her Porsche Boxster. A month into the relationship, he casually mentioned that the last woman he dated paid him $1,000 a month.

That's when she implemented a new rule: "I said, 'From now on, they have to have been born when Kennedy was shot.'"

In 2019, after her 45th high school reunion in Iowa, Haver received an unexpected message from a high school friend. He had missed the reunion, but saw photos of her celebrating and reached out. "He, for some reason, just decided to look me up on Classmates.com of all places," she said with a shudder. "Horrible, horrible site," she said.

The online user experience was bad, but the conversation was good.

"I would get in great political discussions with him, because he was a dyed-in-the-wool Republican and I was as far from that as possible, especially now," Haver said. They married four years ago.

For other women we spoke to, political disagreement did not translate to romantic frisson. Pearson Brown, 63, recently ended a 10-year postdivorce relationship with a man over political differences.

"I knew his politics were different than mine, and we never really discussed politics very much," Brown said from her home in Warrenton, Virginia, where she works in pharmaceutical PR and advertising. "But as my primary partner, I'd say 'Groceries are high' or 'Gas is [expensive]' and it would become a political conversation. 'Pass the salt' became a political statement," she said.

In February of this year, it became too much. They went their separate ways.

The experience changed the way she now approaches online dating. "Some people say, 'No MAGA' and I'm like, 'Okay, fine,'" Brown said. "Before, I used to say, 'I don't like anybody saying "No something."' No fat, no smoke, whatever. But now I'm like, 'Okay, I just saved myself some time.'"

How much should you compromise as a woman dating later in life? And how much should you stand firm on?

"At this point, I have my house, I have my own space, I have my life," said Lacey Wootton, who retired from her job as a professor at American University in May 2025.

"It sounds small and petty, but I don't think it is: I have dinner when I want to have dinner, and if I want to watch something on TV, I do, or if I want to sit and read, I do," Wootton, 66, said. "And I have closet space."

Wootton agreed she sounded a little like Carol Burnett, who once told Joan Rivers, "If I ever got married again, he would have to live next door."

She's currently dating, and she's enjoyed some relationships with men that have lasted a few months. But her standards are high for settling down.

"If, by chance, I met someone who was really amazing, I would think about that compromise," she said. "But I'm also not hunting."

Wootton divorced amicably from her husband when she was 50. "I was really scared of being alone," Wootton said. But gradually, she acclimated to single life. Very well. Now, 16 years later, she's never been happier. She volunteers, she goes to the theater, she reads voraciously, and she has a circle of friends who share her interests. When we spoke, she was hours away from flying to Scandinavia for a two-week adventure.

She's not interested in a romantic partner who can't keep up. "Men age more than women, and I don't want to be a 72-year-old nursemaid," she said.

Wootton has also found that age does not necessarily bring maturity. She's been ghosted and flaked on more times than she can count. "Some of those habits that older people maybe ascribe to younger people in terms of digital behavior, our age group does it, too," she said.

Keep an open mind, but watch for red flags

Online dating, it seems, can be unpleasant regardless of age. But Amy Schoen, a dating coach in Bethesda who caters to boomers, still thinks that the apps are the best way for seniors to meet each other.

"Eighty percent of my successful clients have met through online dating," Schoen said. The problem, she says, isn't the app itself but what your profile is communicating.

"You have to put your goals out there, that's the number one thing on the profile," said Schoen, 66. She advises her clients to think of their profile as a "30-second infomercial" that clearly lists five to seven characteristics that you're looking for in a partner. She also recommends that her clients share these traits with their friends so that they can act as "scouts" to round up potential matches.

The most serious challenge Schoen's clients face is online romance scammers who target single women. Part of her coaching involves looking out for red flags like refusing to meet in person or on video, love bombing, and introducing financial discussions early in the relationship. Of course, safety is the most important concern when it comes to dating at any age.

But Schoen also advises her clients to keep an open mind. After her own divorce, Schoen found great solace in the support group New Beginnings. She also discovered several new social groups, including Bike & Brunch, where she met her current husband. Schoen is a self-starter, a go-getter, a people person. Her husband is more introverted. She's glad she didn't let that stop her from dating him.

"One of the biggest mistakes people make is to be judgmental," Schoen said. Some of the most successful senior relationships she's seen have been between people from different backgrounds, different religions and different socioeconomic statuses.

"My clients who have a sense of adventure, who are willing to try things and go out there and expand their world seem to do better as a whole," she said. She has clients who ended up married but living separately. Others fell in love with partners who didn't seem compatible on paper. Some are dating with significant age gaps. And some of her clients are happy to just have fun.

"Now they're dating for themselves and their own enjoyment and their own needs," Schoen said. "Many people have been like, 'I've been there for my kids, I've been there for my partner, now it's my turn.'"

Some seniors are wilder than others. For some boomers, the counterculture never straightened out and the sexual revolution never stopped revolving.

"I can tell you, there are girls in their mid-80s who are still in circulation, right?" said Renée Imperato, 78, from her apartment in Manhattan. "They're still bumping the hump, you hear me?"

When she was in her 20s, Imperato mostly dated older men. That is no longer the case.

"Sometimes younger people say, 'Renée, you're the queen, you're our elder, where are all the other people in your age group?'" said the retired Air Force veteran and longtime transgender rights activist. "And you know what my answer is? One word: AIDS."

Imperato has been married four times and has dated people of many genders. These days she "predominantly" identifies as a trans lesbian. She has "T4T" tattooed on her neck, signaling her preference for dating other trans people. And she's currently dating a couple several decades her junior. When we spoke, she was recovering from a foot injury and shingles. She refuses to let such things slow her down.

"Listen, honey, as long as I can do what I can do, I'm going to do it until I can't," Imperato said.

articles.title: 'Nationally significant' solar farm near Newark approved by government
articles.summary: Developers say the Great North Road Solar Park has the potential to power up to 400,000 homes.
articles.body:
Plans for a major solar farm classed as "nationally significant infrastructure" has been approved by the government's Planning Inspectorate.

The Great North Road Solar and Biodiversity Park, near Newark in Nottinghamshire, has the potential to power up to 400,000 homes - the equivalent of every home in the county - developers Elements Green previously said .

The project would form a ring of "solar islands" roughly 6.2 miles (10km) from north to south around villages such as Caunton and Ossington, with the eastern edge alongside the A1.

Final approval was given by Baroness Margaret Curran on behalf of the secretary of state for energy security and net-zero.

Its nationally significant classification meant the applicant was required to apply for consent from the Planning Inspectorate rather than Newark and Sherwood District Council.

Announcing the decision on Tuesday, the government said the application was for a solar photovoltaic array generating station, battery energy storage system and grid connection infrastructure, with a maximum generation capacity of 800MW.

"The examining authority listened and gave full consideration to all local views and the evidence gathered during the examination before making its recommendation to the secretary of state," a government spokesperson added.

People living nearby had raised concerns over the potential impact the scheme could have on the area, and the results of a consultation published in 2024 showed 54% of respondents opposed it.

Robert Jenrick, Reform UK MP for Newark, said he was "appalled and devastated" by the news, and felt the views of local people had been ignored.

"The whole area will now be subjected to acre upon acre of solar panels," he said.

"More than 10% of my constituency will now be solar. Good farmland ruined. Years of mess and disruption. Views wrecked for generations."

The government's decision can be challenged in the High Court, which would make a decision on whether there would be grounds for a judicial review.

This process would have to happen within six weeks.

articles.title: HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final: Field, format and prize purse as players battle for DP World Tour promotion in Mallorca
articles.summary: Key questions about the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final and the Road to Mallorca Rankings, where platers look secure DP World Tour status for next season; watch the first round live on Sky Sports from 11am on Thursday
articles.body:
What is the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final and the Road to Mallorca Rankings?

This year's event marks the 31st time the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final has been played and will bring the curtain down on the DP World Tour feeder circuit's 28-event season.

It will also conclude the HotelPlanner Tour's points competition, the Road to Mallorca Rankings, with the top-45 golfers in the standings set to tee up this week in hopes of securing a coveted DP World Tour card for next season.

James Morrison won the event in 2025, while JC Ritchie topped the Road to Mallorca Rankings.

Club de Golf Alcanada, situated on Mallorca's south-east coast, has hosted the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final for the past five years and is set to stage the 2026 showpiece once again.

At the end of the tournament, the top 15 players in the Road to Mallorca standings will be awarded a DP World Tour card for next season.

And we're set for a thrilling finale, with every player in the 45-man field able to earn promotion to the DP World Tour.

Four-thousand Road to Mallorca Rankings Points are up for grabs, with the winner of the Grand Final awarded 640 points. Second place will claim 440 points and third will secure 280 points.

American Alex Goff is the lowest-ranked player in the field on 447.30 points. Meanwhile, England's Matthew Southgate sits in the final DP World Tour qualifying spot. The pair are separated by 243.55 points, meaning Goff could jump into the top 15 with a win.

A £418,000 (€500,000) prize fund is also up for grabs.

Tapio Pulkkanen , enters the tournament fifth in the Road to Mallorca standings and is bidding to become the first player to have won the HotelPlanner Tour's order of merit twice, after he finished No 1 in 2017.

Current Road to Mallorca Rankings leader, Hamish Brown , will have his sights set on holding down the No 1 spot. Brown comes into the week in good form after winning the tour's penultimate event, the Hangzhou Open, on October 18.

Swedish golfer Christofer Blomstrand and Lars Van der Vight trail him in second, and third place and will both be keen to leapfrog Brown to snatch the No 1 spot.

Chris Wood , who featured at the 2016 Ryder Cup, is looking to return to the DP World Tour after losing his playing rights in 2022. Wood, who competed in the LIV Golf Promotions event in January, comes into the Grand Final ranked No 37.

Three other former LIV Golfers are in the field this week, including Frederik Kjetterup , who was relegated from LIV Golf in 2025 after signing for Cleeks GC in 2024.

Dominic Foos and John Catlin , who also featured in January's LIV Golf Promotions event, come into the event ranked 31st and 41st in the rankings.

Many European golfing stars have graduated to the DP World Tour following victories at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final, including Thomas Bjorn in 1995, Edoardo Molinari in 2009 and Tommy Fleetwood in 2011.

More recently, Ryder Cup hopefuls Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen won at Club de Golf Alcanada in 2023 and 2024, respectively.

articles.title: Historic Scottish golf course submerged by Storm Boelo flooding, faces extensive damage
articles.summary: Dumbarton Golf Club faces a long recovery after Storm Boelo left the historic course completely underwater.
articles.body:
A Scottish golf course has issued an update on its future after Storm Boelo submerged it over the weekend.

Aerial photos taken Tuesday show the golf course almost completely underwater, and the club says the damage is "difficult to imagine right now."

Founded in 1888, Dumbarton Golf Club is a historic 18-hole parkland course in the heart of the town, regarded as one of the oldest golf clubs in the west of Scotland.

The club's management team said they wanted to provide an update after "the devastation from Saturday night" and thanked those who got in touch to offer help.

They said: "We are monitoring the water coming in from the collapsed embankment as this will not be a quick fix. We have liaised with West Dunbartonshire Council, and their priority is, rightly, to close the towpath for safety reasons. They will then review the situation with engineers, but there is no guidance on timescales for this.

"Therefore, we are left to try and do what we can to get the water off the course as quickly as possible. This will probably result in extra pumps being required at our cost. We are currently trying to secure these.

"The damage to the course once the water has receded is difficult to imagine right now.

"Bunkers may all need to be re-sanded, multiple bridges will need to be rebuilt, debris will take time to remove, and there are a number of damaged trees that we cannot get to. This will result in a significant cost as well."

The management team went on to say they have decided to reduce the club's operating hours to save money.

They added: "This is heartbreaking, given that we have been doing so much in the clubhouse. We would ask members to support the club wherever possible and follow the revised opening hours, which will be sent out regularly.

"We have received offers of help from various nearby golf courses. This has been extremely welcome, and we thank Helensburgh Golf Club, Cardross Golf Club and Clydebank and District Golf Club for reaching out to us at this time.

"This is still very much an ongoing situation, and we will try to update you as we know more. Please bear with us as much as possible."

The update came after we reported on Tuesday afternoon that the yellow warning for high winds covering the whole of Scotland and the far north-east of Northern Ireland has been cut short.

Forecasters now predict the bad weather will end at 6 p.m., three hours earlier than expected.

Storm-hit communities across Scotland are asking "serious questions" as politicians say "significant lessons" must be learned from the devastation left by Storm Boelo.

Storm Boelo pummelled the north of the UK over the weekend, bringing 84mph gusts and a third of a month's rain to pockets of Scotland.

Richard Baines, curator of Logan Botanic Garden, was killed after being hit by a falling tree during the storm.

The 60-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene at Mid Kelton near Castle Douglas around 10.30 a.m. on Sunday morning.

articles.title: Tiger Woods' Timeline to Return from Back Injury Reportedly Revealed Ahead of 2026-27 TGL Season
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is reportedly nearing a return to competitive golf.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is reportedly nearing a return to competitive golf.

ESPN's Mark Schlabach reported Tuesday that Woods is "expected" to play for the Jupiter Links Golf Club in the Dec. 27 opener of TGL's third season if there are no further setbacks. He participated in just one TGL match during the 2026 season due to back surgery.

What's more, his last appearance in a PGA Tour tournament was in 2024.

The Dec. 27 opener will feature a high-profile doubleheader with Woods and the Jupiter Links Golf Club facing Los Angeles Golf Club in a rematch of last season's finals.

It will be an opportunity for some revenge, as Los Angeles won last season's title.

That will be the second match after Brooks Kopeka makes his TGL debut with Motor City Golf Club. They face Boston Common Golf, which features Rory McIlroy.

As for Woods, Schlabach noted the TGL opener could be part of a busy December for the all-time great.

It remains to be seen whether he will compete in the Hero World Challenge that he hosts in the Bahamas. What's more, he could play alongside his son, Charlie, in the PNC Championship, especially since he was granted permission to use a cart in the 36-hole event.

Woods is on the short list of the best golfers in the history of the sport and counts 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour tournament victories on his illustrious resume. However, injuries and surgeries have been a significant issue in the latter portion of his career.

The 50-year-old will surely never reach the level he did at his peak, but he is still one of the biggest names in all of sports and would generate plenty of interest in the TGL event if he does participate.

articles.title: Jordan Love, Packers offense must avoid familiar trap against Panthers
articles.summary: Jordan Love must be ready to play a boring game against a Carolina defense which keeps everything in front of them, rather than hunting explosives.
articles.body:
When the Green Bay Packers hosted the Carolina Panthers a year ago, they entered the game coming off a 35-point performance on offense on the road in Pittsburgh, only to score 13 in a surprising loss at Lambeau Field.

As they prepare to face the same Ejiro Evero defense on Thursday night, Jordan Love and Green Bay's offense must not fall into the same trap that led to their defeat in 2025.

Carolina's defense is not impressive overall, ranking 20th in the NFL in expected points added (EPA) per play. What they do excel in though is preventing explosive pass plays, where they rank third in the league with only 2.8% of passes turning into 20-plus yard plays.

That was the case last year too, as Evero's defensive ideology strives to keep everything in front of them. Jordan Love could not help but get bored, leading to him forcing downfield throws and making mistakes in the loss.

After posting a 134.1 passer rating against the Steelers a week earlier, he dropped down to 80.1 versus the Panthers, throwing one interception and zero touchdowns.

Perhaps even more so this year, the Packers survive on explosives in the passing game, ranking second in the league at 7%. It is a bad matchup for how Green Bay wants (or needs) to operate on offense.

They have had no run game to speak of during the first seven games, and a combination of uneven offensive line play, drops and other concentration or execution errors, they are not the type of team that can consistently go on long drives by taking what the defense gives them.

That is the formula they will need to embrace on Thursday night, and it may be reliant on getting the run game going, which is a terrifying thought.

Carolina ranks 26th in explosive run rate, so even if Josh Jacobs cannot consistently grind out yards, ripping off some chunk plays could be important. He averaged 5.1 yards per carry against them last year.

Another crucial element the Packers could lean on is Tucker Kraft, who tore his ACL in this same fixture last season.

It is possible the game plan a year ago was to channel the offense through Kraft against such a soft defense, given his ability to pick up yards after the catch. He is yet to produce an explosive performance like the ones he did in 2025, and Thursday night would be a good time to do so.

Matt LaFleur knows Ejero well after working with him at previous stops and even interviewing him for the Packers defensive coordinator job when he ended up hiring Joe Barry instead. He knows what to expect.

LaFleur said: "I think it's a very tough defense to go against because they're going to try to keep a lid on you and they're going to make you earn it, so you've gotta be consistent with, not just one person, all eleven have gotta be consistent throughout. You've gotta stay patient."

Thursday presents an opportunity for Love and the Packers to prove they can put up points the long way, and if they fail that test, it may be decisive in another loss.

articles.title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 8
articles.summary: Where do the Texans fall following their overtime loss to the Giants?
articles.body:
So much for that win in London! Following Houston's fantastic victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars one week ago to improve to 2-4, last Sunday's game against the New York Giants was supposed to be another step back towards contention. Instead, both Houston's offense and defense fell back on their old habits of poor blocking and poor tackling, penalties galore, and the like as the Texans lost to the Giants 27-21 in overtime. This loss practically wiped out any hopes for a comeback season in Houston, giving the team a record of 2-5 and with some serious questions to answer during the bye week.

One of the most stunning developments of this game was Giants QB J.J. McCarthy, who was starting his first game with New York after being traded by the Minnesota Vikings. He was such a colossal disappointment in Minnesota that head coach Kevin O'Connel went from drafting him tenth overall in 2024, to the birth of "nine" in 2025 after multiple grizzly performances, to demoting him to third-stringer in 2026 – behind QB Carson Wentz! Today marks a month since the Giants decided to deal a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings for McCarthy, and they are looking like geniuses for that decision. In his first start since Minnesota's 2025 regular season finale against the Green Bay Packers, McCarthy demolished what little reputation the Texans' defense had left from last year, repeatedly targeting Giants star WR Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields, who both combined for 11 receptions and 194 yards on just 14 targets. They practically embarassed the entire Texans' secondary with those two receivers, which alone should give you idea on how far the Texans have fallen, especially without S Jalen Pitre on the field.

And once you get over the J.J. McCarthy angle of this loss, it only gets worse from there! Giants RBs Cam Skattebo and (former Texan) Devin Singletary gashed Houston's defense over and over again, both finishing the game with a combined 165 rushing yards and two touchdowns on just 22 carries. Practically all of the Giants' RBs were placed in the doghouse by head coach John Harbaugh last week as he aired his frustrations over their issues thus far, and the Texans defense became the catalyst to their "get right" game! Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary – a RB that the Texans' coaching staff and defense should know how to stop from his year here in 2023 – had their bounce back games against the Houston Texans! And RT Jermaine Eluemunor was gassed up in the Giants locker room postgame, too:

Maybe it's fitting the Texans lose like this a week before Halloween, because this might as well be a nightmare come to life! The shadow cast by Houston's losing record grows ever longer as the days grow shorter, and the sense that time is running out climbs up their minds as a chill raises the hairs on their backs. At 2-5, Houston's fight or flight response has been activated, but has the air of desperation come too late for these Texans? Well, let's take a look at where everyone is ranking them following their 27-21 overtime loss to the New York Giants:

18. Houston Texans (2-5) (Last Week: 22)

Another tough loss has landed on the Texans' ledger, reducing their room for error going forward. It's fair to say this defense is no longer deserving of its respected reputation — especially when reflecting on how Devin Singletary ran right through the heart of the unit to a game-winning touchdown . I do believe C.J. Stroud will continue to keep Houston competitive. I'm keeping an eye on that connection with Marvin Harrison Jr. too; Stroud's touchdown pass to his former Ohio State teammate on Sunday was exquisite.

Week 7 result: Lost to the Giants 27-21 (OT) Week 7 ranking: 16

Best offseason addition: TE Foster Moreau

The Texans didn't have many big offseason acquisitions, but Moreau has provided help in the run game. And he has been a good red zone threat with three total touchdowns. Moreau has played 43% of the snaps, eating into the playing time of tight end Dalton Schultz , who is down from 70% in 2025 to 57% this season. Moreau helps Houston's offense not be predictable when he's in the game. Even though Houston has just two wins, its offense is averaging 24 points per game. And Moreau is a noteworthy part of the unit.

Last week's ranking: No. 14 Last week's result: lost to Giants, 27–21 (OT) This week: idle

I know great defenses are difficult to maintain from year to year, but the Texans' fall from grace remains one of the most stunning moments in recent history. J.J. McCarthy would have been ripped to shreds by almost the exact same cast of characters a year ago (no offense). How do you not evolve over the course of an offseason?

Week 7 Result: Lost vs. New York Giants 27-21 (OT)

Back-to-back wins briefly revived Houston's season. Sunday's loss exposed how much work remains.

There are a number of reasons why the Texans have struggled, but the most surprising has to be the team's defensive collapse. Last year, Houston led the league in total defense and ranked first in the AFC in scoring defense. This season, Houston's defense has been average—on a good day.

The Texans allowed 420 yards of offense in Sunday's overtime loss, including 188 yards and four scores on the ground.

The offense isn't without blame—taking on a Giants team short its best edge-rusher and green-dot linebacker, Houston had just 237 yards of offense and was 3-for-12 on third down.

The Texans head into their bye week facing an unpleasant reality: There will be no return to the playoffs in 2026.

Losing at home to the Giants just might be the death blow in their chances of winning the AFC South. The defense just isn't good enough.

24. Houston Texans (20): It may be a lost season in H-Town, but not if you're Tank Dell. Welcome back, boss, and props.

The Texans' loss Sunday was one of the most damaging of the entire NFL season. They were double-digit favorites to beat the Giants, and a win over New York would have put Houston at 3-4, not far behind 4-2 Jacksonville with a head-to-head win over the Jaguars. And the Texans had a massive letdown in an overtime loss to the Giants. At 2-5, their margin of error is incredibly slim with 10 games to go.

At this point it's clear the Texans are nowhere near as good on defense as expected. They were 16th in defensive DVOA through Sunday's games and 24th in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed. Needing a stop in overtime Sunday, Houston allowed runs of 42 and 30 yards on back-to-back plays that ended the game.

"No magical elixir is going to drop out of the sky and … fix it," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said according to AP. "We fix it by putting the work in and getting better at fundamentals of football and that's where we've got to just own it. As coaches, as players, we've all got to own it and we've got to find a way to turn this thing around."

The Texans were supposed to be Super Bowl contenders. Their defense was supposed to be among the best in the NFL. Instead, the unit ranks 24th in EPA per play and has gone from generating the second-most pressure in the league to the ninth most.

23. Texans (No. 19; 2-5): Has an elite defense ever fallen apart this quickly?

Average Ranking: 21.44 (Last Week: 16.78)

Sports Illustrated analyst Conor Orr was one of the last pundits listed here that was clinging on to the concept of a Texans comeback this year, but now even he has given up. Orr was all-in on the Texans this year, writing a big piece on their defense back in August, pairing that story with a massive cover shoot of DE Will Anderson Jr., and declaring they would go 13-4 and win the Super Bowl this season! Following this long, Orr had this to say on the Heed the Call Podcast:

"We talked a couple weeks ago about how, uh, if you had an "ugly baby," or you didn't like it, you could put it in the German, uh, in the "German Drawer" and it just goes away forever. I'm putting it in…I'm putting the Texans in the drawer. I'm getting rid of them, they're done. It was a baby – I loved it, I brought it into this world, um, but um, I'm finished taking of it. I'm good." – Conor Orr, NFL Week 7 Recap of EVERY Game!, Heed the Call Podcast

Going from the preseason Super Bowl winner to a "German Drawer" not even halfway through the season? Well…yeah, that about sums it up for me, too. This was about as close to a "dream team" I think the Texans have ever had, and, despite the midseason adjustments they've made, are truly a bad football team. ESPN is still giving the Texans a 23.6% chance of making the playoffs largely because of how comparatively easy their remaining schedule is, but following this loss to the Giants, I don't know if the Texans can be trusted to beat anyone.

Like many bad teams, the avenues to defeating the Texans seem to be growing by the week, and nothing about their team can be deemed "consistent" besides their poor run-blocking and tackling. On the flip side on Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor's great game was Texans LT Aireontae Ersery's bad game, giving up multiple pressures, penalties, and once again being a non-factor in the rushing attack. On the flip side of LB Azeez Al-Shaair's poor tackling performance was Giants' rookie LB Arvell Reese's second game with 5+ tackles, a tackle-for-loss, and a QB hit. You could play this game all over the field when comparing the Giants and Texans, as there were a lot of players on Houston's roster that deserve a share of the blame for this loss.

I was a bit more suspicious of the Texans coming into the regular season because of a rash of injuries that ran through the team throughout the offseason and their (in my view) mediocre draft haul back in April, but even I wasn't expecting a collapse this dramatic. This game was supposed to provide some answers to those desperate for the team to get back on track, and instead, there are now only more questions. QB CJ Stroud may have saved the team from a crisis last week, but that optimism was very, very short lived.

What do you think, though? Are the Texans still capable of mounting a comeback following their bye week, or will things only stand to get worse until bigger changes are made? Will this season become a big enough meltdown that job security will be a question for Nick Caley, Matt Burke, DeMeco Ryans, or even Nick Caserio? Do any of these staffers deserve the blame, or are there players the Texans should be prepared to move on from following this year's horrifying start? At this point, should the Texans even entertain the idea of copying the Indianapolis Colts and becoming a "dealer" at the trade deadline? Let us know your thoughts down in the comments below!

The PGA Tour makes a quick turn from Port Royal in Bermuda to Vidanta Vallarta this week, where the Mexico Open will be contested for a $6 million purse and crucial FedExCup points for fall players looking to secure 2027 playing status.

Brian Campbell is the defending champion but you'll have to scroll quite a ways down to find his odds to win outright (+22500).

The pretournament favorite is Wyndham Clark, a three-time winner on Tour this season including his second U.S. Open crown in June at Shinnecock.

Here's a look at where Clark and the rest of the field stand ahead of the Tour's fifth fall event and first of two stops in Mexico.

VidantaWorld Mexico Open odds (as of Wednesday, Oct. 28, courtesy of DraftKings)

When handicapping a tournament it's hard to tell where the line between bias against landing on the favorite outright ends and the desire to chase perceived value begins. The Mexico Open is perhaps the best juxtaposition of these two equally limited preconceptions in the 2026 Tour schedule.

And this wasn't a situation anyone could have planned for but here we are: The weather in Bermuda over the weekend has created a certain level of randomness because of travel (see: chaos) that theoretically is ideal for a longshot to sneak in and topple what seems to be a top-heavy field . Add in the desperation that comes with the fall golf season, and the conditions are right for something shocking to happen south of the border.

The opening round of the VidantaWorld Mexico Open is underway at Vidanta Vallarta Golf Course in Vallarta, Mexico.

But ... digging into the numbers suggests that oddsmakers might actually be doing a disservice to Clark at +1325. We make him more of a 7-to-1 favorite based on his elite approach game compared to the field. Additionally, he's kept it superbly clean with the putter in 2026 — placing him No. 8 in strokes gained total. There are only two other players inside the top 30 teeing off this week: co-second favorites Tom Kim and Doug Ghim .

Ghim was going to be our pick before crunching all the data on Clark. And it's hard to root against (see: pick against) Kim at this point after what he did in his native South Korea three weeks ago , therefore we'll offer all three up as recommended plays to win.

Editor's note: Ghim has leapt up from an opening number of +3500 on Sunday to being tied as the second favorite as of Wednesday afternoon.

Not to make this a pure strokes gained total gush fest but we had circled Keita Nakajima's name similarly to Ghim before putting in some research. As it turns out, Nakajima ranks two spots behind fourth favorite Ben Griffin in that category and is given more than double the odds pretournament so we'll gladly pull the trigger on Nakakima at +4400 as he's better than Griffin off the tee and on the green this year. All of that spells value!

And for those who think that number to win is a bit short for a player in search of his first PGA Tour win, we encourage a pick to place as the 26-year-old Japanese native sits 129th in fall points and needs to climb inside the top 125 to improve his conditional status next year.

Four more in this top 10 opening round market who have fair enough numbers that are worth a look: Kevin Yu (+580), Austin Eckroa t (+610), Max Greyserman (+630) and Tony Finau (+650). Great, now we have a "starting lineup."
